  "title": "Trump Seeks Iran Peace Talks With China and Russia Despite Reports of Their Military Support for Tehran",
  "deck": "American intelligence assessments reportedly identified Chinese and Russian military assistance to Iran. President Trump now expects to discuss ending the war with both countries' leaders in Shenzhen.",
  image: {
    src: "assets/images/epnews_trump_iran_peace.png",
    "alt": "AI-generated editorial illustration of Trump, Xi and Putin with Iranian flag",
    "credit": "EP News / AI-generated editorial illustration"
  },
  "body": [
    "President Donald Trump is preparing for a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin that could bring three of the world's most powerful countries into discussions over ending the war in Iran.",
    "Senior American officials told ABC News on November 13 that the leaders would meet during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China. Nuclear arms control is expected to dominate the discussion, with Iran also on the agenda.",
    "The meeting presents Washington with a difficult diplomatic problem. The two governments Trump hopes can help end the conflict have reportedly provided military assistance to Tehran during the war.",
    "What American intelligence reportedly found",
    "On October 12, Trump publicly dismissed suggestions that China and Russia were assisting Iran.",
    "He said he did not believe either country was helping Tehran and suggested any assistance would be limited.",
    "Reuters reported the following day that American intelligence assessments had identified military support from both countries, including satellite imagery used for targeting and weapons components. The report cited two people briefed on the intelligence.",
    "The underlying assessments have not been made public, limiting independent verification of their findings.",
    "The reported assistance nevertheless raises questions about the relationship between Washington's diplomatic strategy and its assessment of the countries supporting Iran.",
    "Washington had already warned Beijing",
    "Trump's October remarks followed a September meeting with Xi at the White House.",
    "U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue said afterward that Trump had warned Beijing against providing intelligence, military equipment or other assistance to Iran. Perdue said Washington received assurances from Chinese officials.",
    "Reuters separately reported that a senior Iranian official said Beijing had assured Tehran that it would maintain its economic, political and military relationships with Iran.",
    "Those accounts leave unresolved whether the assurances given to Washington resulted in meaningful changes to Chinese assistance.",
    "China's economic relationship with Iran",
    "China's importance to Tehran extends beyond military supplies.",
    "Reuters reported in September that Iran had used a barter-like arrangement to circumvent restrictions on its oil sales and acquire billions of dollars in Chinese goods, including military equipment.",
    "These arrangements can allow Tehran to obtain supplies without relying entirely on conventional international payment channels.",
    "Washington has targeted Chinese independent oil refineries and intermediaries involved in Iranian petroleum trade. However, a November 16 analysis from the Jewish Institute for National Security of America argued that broader Chinese financial networks remain insufficiently targeted.",
    "China also has substantial reasons to seek an end to the fighting. Disruption in the Strait of Hormuz threatens its energy imports and commercial interests throughout the Persian Gulf.",
    "Earlier this year, the Associated Press reported that Beijing had used its influence with Tehran to encourage a ceasefire.",
    "Chinese economic support for Iran and Chinese participation in peace efforts can therefore coexist.",
    "Russia's competing interests",
    "Moscow maintains its own strategic relationship with Tehran while competing with Washington over European security and global influence.",
    "Higher energy prices can benefit Russian petroleum exporters. A prolonged Middle Eastern conflict can also divert American attention and military resources from other regions.",
    "These potential advantages do not establish that Russia wants the war to continue indefinitely. Moscow has warned that the conflict could contribute to nuclear proliferation in the Middle East.",
    "Russia may also see diplomatic participation as an opportunity to strengthen its international position and negotiate with Washington on other issues.",
    "Who holds the leverage?",
    "The Shenzhen meeting could reveal whether Washington can persuade Beijing and Moscow to use their relationships with Tehran to advance a settlement.",
    "Both countries have channels of influence that the United States lacks. Their commercial and strategic relationships with Iran could make them useful participants in negotiations.",
    "Those same relationships could complicate American efforts to restrict Iran's military capabilities.",
    "The distinction will matter after any ceasefire. Ending immediate hostilities would not necessarily prevent Tehran from replenishing military equipment or restoring its financial networks.",
    "The November 19 meeting is expected to be an initial discussion rather than a venue for a comprehensive agreement.",
    "Whether it produces meaningful progress will depend in part on what China and Russia are prepared to change in their relationships with Iran, and what Washington is willing to offer in return."
  ],

    },

    },
    {
      "label": "JINSA - November 16 analysis",
      "url": "https://jinsa.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Trump-Russia-China-Insight-11.16.2026.pdf"
    },
    {
      "label": "Associated Press - summit confirmation",
      "url": "https://apnews.com/article/5fe92253ef38100bae913834a9b74d72"
    }
  ]

reel.headline: Trump Seeks Iran Peace Talks With China and Russia Despite Reports of Their Military Support for Tehran
reel.facebook_description: Trump is expected to discuss Iran with Xi and Putin in Shenzhen. Reuters reported in October that U.S. intelligence assessments identified military assistance from both countries, even as Trump disputed such support. Follow EP News for evidence-led reporting.
